root_idea.summary: A root oriented toward elevation, forceful restoration, and bringing something back to upright or sound condition.
root_idea.development: The lexical development runs from setting a fractured bone and restoring what is damaged to restoring a person's condition, while force and elevation yield the senses of compelling, dominating, being lofty, and being unreachable.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The single QAC group is a Quran-attested lexical form and is presented under the normalized citation form جَبَّار.

senses.definition: A self-exalting, arrogant, insolent, and rebellious person who refuses the truth or proper submission.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of human beings as a condemnatory description of pride, defiance, and refusal to accept correction or obedience.

senses.definition: One who overpowers or compels others by force; an overbearing tyrant.
senses.usage_conditions: Describes coercive domination of others, including the sense of one who cannot be compelled by ordinary human authority.

senses.definition: The Supreme and Irresistibly Powerful One, exalted above and beyond the reach of creatures.
senses.usage_conditions: A divine designation; its force and elevation are not the condemned human qualities of the preceding senses.

senses.definition: The Restorer who repairs deficiency and supports or strengthens those in need.
senses.usage_conditions: A divine interpretation of the designation, emphasizing restoration through abundant power and provision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To set a broken bone, reduce it from a fractured state, or restore it to sound condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively for the bone-setter's action and in related usage of a bone becoming set or restored.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To restore a person, orphan, poor man, or other thing from deficiency or damage to a sound, sufficient, or good condition; to confer the benefit that repairs a lack.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or extended restoration sense, including recovery from poverty or embarrassment and putting affairs right.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To compel or constrain someone, against his will, to do something or to submit to a judgment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction جَبَرَهُ عَلَى is used for coercion; the lexical idea is forceful imposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impute to someone the doctrine of جَبْر, or to call him a partisan of that doctrine.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized denominational use, distinct from ordinary physical or personal compulsion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recover what had been lost, regain a good condition, or return to growth and vigor; of a plant, to become green and put forth fresh shoots after drying or being eaten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or middle restoration sense applied to people, property, health, and vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To magnify oneself and behave proudly, haughtily, or insolently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reflexive or self-directed expression of arrogant conduct.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To acquire wealth or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended intransitive use reported for the derived verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To recover from a calamity or from a condition from which recovery is difficult.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction of a calamity that cannot be recovered from, with the negative expressing the absence of recovery.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exert oneself greatly in caring for someone or in putting that person's affairs into proper condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A causative-seeking construction focused on sustained attention and repair of another's circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An addition or completion made in calculation to repair or complete an amount; hence algebra.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical mathematical use, including the expression الجَبْرُ وَالمُقَابَلَةُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The theological doctrine that human beings are compelled by God in their actions, denying independent voluntary efficacy to them.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A post-classical technical theological term, contrasted with قَدَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A king; also, in reported contrasting nominal uses, a slave or servant, a man, a young man, or a courageous man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: These are lexical nominal applications reported under the same form and include explicitly contrasting senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Possibly aloes-wood.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tentative and textually uncertain identification in the lexical tradition; it may reflect a corrupted explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Self-magnification, pride, haughtiness, or insolent behavior—the quality associated with a جَبَّار.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun for the disposition or conduct of arrogant domination, distinct from the name of the theological sect.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The theological sect or doctrine asserting that human beings have no independent power and are compelled in their actions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical post-classical designation, with variant pronunciations and forms reported in the tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The proper name of the angel Gabriel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A foreign or compound proper name with numerous dialectal and orthographic variants.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A matter for which no retaliation, blood compensation, or other monetary liability is exacted; a death or injury treated as unavenged or uncompensated.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in legal and customary expressions concerning wells, mines, wars, wounds, and injuries caused by an unattended animal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clear or quit of a matter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the idiomatic expression أَنَا مِنْهُ خَلَاوَةٌ وَجُبَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A torrent, or anything that corrupts, mars, and destroys.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The torrent sense may be extended to a destructive force or to something destroyed by such a force.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tuesday.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An ancient name used in the pre-Islamic period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A splint or piece of wood used to set a broken bone or restore a diseased part to sound condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its plural is جَبَائِر; the related form جَبِيرَةٌ is also reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wide bracelet or armlet of gold or silver.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ornament sense is associated by resemblance with a splint; related usage includes a smooth armlet or bracelet.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A name for the constellation Orion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative naming based on its representation as a crowned king on a throne.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In ذِرَاعُ الجَبَّارِ, the cubit of a king or a long cubit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional measurement expression; the term may refer to a foreign king whose forearm was unusually long.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A heart that does not accept admonition or admit compassion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description of hardness and imperviousness of heart.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm tree, tall, young, and beyond the reach of the hand.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a single palm or collectively to palms; the feminine form may denote a young palm that has reached full height and borne fruit.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Huge, tall, and strong; a giant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended descriptive use for exceptional size and strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a she-camel, great and fat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal-specific application is explicitly reported for this adjective.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bread or a preparation of bruised and cooked grain; also the ear of corn in a related expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized food name, including the expressions جَابِرُ بْنُ حَبَّةَ and أَبُو جَابِرٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who exerts himself greatly in caring for someone or restoring that person's affairs to proper condition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the construction فُلَانٌ جَابِرٌ لِي.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bone-setter, one who sets bones or reduces fractures.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial occupational noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman possessed by a jinn, equivalent in the cited usage to a madwoman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare and explicitly weakly attested lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The lion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized animal name associated with forceful or domineering behavior.

cautions: جَبَّارٌ is used in the Quran both negatively for human arrogance or coercive domination and positively as a divine designation; the surrounding subject determines the sense.
The divine designation has both compulsion/supremacy and restoration interpretations in the supplied lexical evidence; these should not be reduced to the ordinary human sense.
The aloes-wood meaning of جَبْرٌ is explicitly tentative and may reflect textual corruption.
The meaning مَجْبُورَةٌ ‘woman possessed by a jinn’ is reported as weakly attested.
